newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Gov. scraps call for sales tax renewal.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Gov. scraps call for sales tax renewal.

text.p: With Louisiana revenues exceeding projections, Gov. Mike Foster has abandoned plans to seek renewal of a one-cent sales tax on food and utilities that expires on June 30, the Advocate newspaper said Thursday.
Foster and legislative leaders said the state can afford to live without the $110 million of annual revenues the tax produces.
Foster did not indicate how much extra revenue the state is expecting from other sources, but said it would be enough to offset the loss of the sales tax.

He had proposed renewing the tax in order to provide money for education. He told the newspaper that extra state revenues will be sufficient to provide $30 million to expand early childhood reading programs and programs for at-risk students, plus $15 million for higher education.
He said it was uncertain whether the additional revenues would be high enough to provide the proposed $65 million for teacher salary raises.

Foster had planned to call a special legislative session in late June to address renewal of the sales tax. He still may call a brief special session to seek reauthorization of a tax-free shopping law scheduled to go off the books on June 30, the newspaper said.
